title: Built a website for train enthusiasts
body:
O.P.
Hi everyone,
Over the last few months I've been building a website called **RailSnap** in my spare time. It started as a personal project to learn more about Next.js and Supabase, but it's gradually turned into something I'd like to grow into a community for Australian rail enthusiasts.
The idea is to have a place where people can:
Upload train sightings with photos
Search by train class, unit number, station or operator
Build a community database of Australia's rolling stock
Comment on and discuss sightings
Browse fleet information and train classes
The site currently supports Melbourne and Sydney train classes, with plans to expand across Australia over time.
Some features I've added recently include:
Multiple photos per sighting
Mobile-friendly interface
User profiles
Duplicate upload prevention
Fleet database and verification tools
Admin dashboard for managing community submissions
It's still in alpha, so I'm expecting there are things that could be improved.
I'm not looking for people to tell me it's great—I'd much rather hear what's confusing, what feels unfinished, or what would stop you from using it. Whether you're into trains or just enjoy trying new web projects, I'd really appreciate honest feedback.
You can have a look here:
https://railsnap.vercel.app
A few questions I'd love feedback on:
Does the interface feel intuitive?
Is there anything that immediately stands out as needing improvement?
If you were building this, what would you focus on next?
Thanks for taking the time to have a look. Any feedback, positive or negative, is genuinely appreciated.
